Representation theory.fact: Representation theory is a branch of mathematics that studies abstract algebraic structures by representing their elements as linear transformations of vector spaces. Rules of engagement.fact: Created for the IIHL by Commander Alan Cole, Major Phillip Drew, Captain Rob McLaughlin and Professor Dennis Mandsager, the San Remo ROE Handbook has been translated from its English original into French, Chinese, Arabic, Spanish, Hungarian, Russian, Bosnian, and Thai and several other languages. Several countries, such as the UK, have used the San Remo Manual as a model for creating their own ROE systems.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The _____ was Sufi mystic and poet (1207–1273).
Rumi.fact: Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī (30 September 1207 – 17 December 1273), commonly called Rumi, was a Sufi mystic, poet, and founder of the Islamic brotherhood called the Mevlevi Order. Rumi is an influential figure in Sufism, and his thought and works loom large both in Persian literature and mystic poetry in general.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī (30 September _____ – 17 December 1273), commonly known as Rumi, was a Sufi mystic, poet, and founder of the Islamic brotherhood known as the Mevlevi Order
Rumi.fact: Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī (30 September 1207 – 17 December 1273), commonly called Rumi, was a Sufi mystic, poet, and founder of the Islamic brotherhood called the Mevlevi Order.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: His family hailed from _____
Rumi.fact: His family hailed from Balkh.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The rapidly advancing _____ hordes forced his family to flee west early on in his life
Rumi.fact: The rapidly advancing Mongol hordes forced his family to flee west early on in his life.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: After spending time in various cities across Iran, _____, and Damascus, he settled in Konya with his family at age 19
Rumi.fact: After spending time in various cities across Iran, Baghdad, and Damascus, he settled in Konya with his family at age 19.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Although he was exposed to Sufi thought from his early childhood, he was expected to follow his fathers footsteps as an _____ scholar
Rumi.fact: Although he was exposed to Sufi thought from his early childhood, he was expected to follow his fathers footsteps as an Islamic scholar.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: However, the arrival to Konya of the mysterious wandering dervish, _____īzī, would alter the course of his life permanently
Rumi.fact: However, the arrival to Konya of the mysterious wandering dervish, Shams Tabrīzī, would alter the course of his life permanently.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: His Masnavi, often called a "Qur'an in _____", is considered one of the greatest poems of the Persian language
Rumi.fact: His Masnavi, often called a "Qur'an in Persian", is considered one of the greatest poems of the Persian language. Many Muslims, particularly in the Turko-Persian cultural sphere, regard the Masnavi as one of the most important works of Islamic literature, falling behind only the Quran.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Many Muslims, particularly in the Turko-_____ cultural sphere, regard the Masnavi as one of the most important works of Islamic literature, falling behind only the Quran
Rumi.fact: His Masnavi, often called a "Qur'an in Persian", is considered one of the greatest poems of the Persian language. Many Muslims, particularly in the Turko-Persian cultural sphere, regard the Masnavi as one of the most important works of Islamic literature, falling behind only the Quran.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: His full name is given by his contemporary Faridun bin _____ as Muhammad bin Muhammad bin al-Husayn al-Khatibi al-Balkhi al-Bakri (Arabic: محمد بن محمد بن الحسين الخطيبي البلخي البكري)
Rumi.fact: His full name is given by his contemporary Faridun bin Ahmad Sipahsalar as Muhammad bin Muhammad bin al-Husayn al-Khatibi al-Balkhi al-Bakri (Arabic: محمد بن محمد بن الحسين الخطيبي البلخي البكري).

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: He is more commonly known as _____ānā Jalāl ad-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī (مولانا جلال‌الدین محمد رومی)
Rumi.fact: He is more commonly called Mawlānā Jalāl ad-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī (مولانا جلال‌الدین محمد رومی).

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Jalal ad-Din is an _____ name meaning "Glory of the Faith"
Rumi.fact: His full name is given by his contemporary Faridun bin Ahmad Sipahsalar as Muhammad bin Muhammad bin al-Husayn al-Khatibi al-Balkhi al-Bakri (Arabic: محمد بن محمد بن الحسين الخطيبي البلخي البكري). Jalal ad-Din is an Arabic name meaning "Glory of the Faith".

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Balkhī and Rūmī are his nisbas, meaning, respectively, "from Balkh" and "from Rûm", as he was from the _____ of Rûm in Anatolia
Rumi.fact: Balkhī and Rūmī are his nisbas, meaning, respectively, "from Balkh" and "from Rûm", as he was from the Sultanate of Rûm in Anatolia.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Mawlānā (مولانا) is a term of _____ origin, meaning "our master"
Rumi.fact: Mawlānā (مولانا) is a term of Arabic origin, meaning "our master". The term مولوی Mawlawī/Mowlavi (Persian) and Mevlevi (Turkish), also of Arabic origin, meaning "my master", is also frequently used for him.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The term مولوی Mawlawī/_____ (Persian) and Mevlevi (Turkish), also of Arabic origin, meaning "my master", is also frequently used for him
Rumi.fact: The term مولوی Mawlawī/Mowlavi (Persian) and Mevlevi (Turkish), also of Arabic origin, meaning "my master", is also frequently used for him.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The area, culturally adjacent to _____, is where Mawlânâ's father, Bahâ' uddîn Walad, was a preacher and jurist
Rumi.fact: The area, culturally adjacent to Balkh, is where Mawlânâ's father, Bahâ' uddîn Walad, was a preacher and jurist. Greater Balkh was at that time a major centre of Persian culture and Sufism had developed there for several centuries.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: He lived and worked there until _____, when Rumi was aged around five and the family moved to Samarkand
Rumi.fact: He lived and worked there until 1212, when Rumi was aged around five and the family moved to Samarkand.

Rumi.fact: The term مولوی Mawlawī/Mowlavi (Persian) and Mevlevi (Turkish), also of Arabic origin, meaning "my master", is also frequently used for him. Greater Balkh was at that time a major centre of Persian culture and Sufism had developed there for several centuries.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: His father was also connected to the spiritual lineage of Najm al-_____
Rumi.fact: His father was also connected to the spiritual lineage of Najm al-Din Kubra.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Rumi lived most of his life under the Persianate Seljuk Sultanate of Rum, where he produced his works and died in _____ AD
Rumi.fact: Rumi lived most of his life under the Persianate Seljuk Sultanate of Rum, where he produced his works and died in 1273 AD.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: He was buried in _____, and his shrine became a place of pilgrimage
Rumi.fact: He was buried in Konya, and his shrine became a place of pilgrimage.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Upon his death, his followers and his son _____ founded the Mevlevi Order, also known as the Order of the Whirling Dervishes, famous for the Sufi dance known as the Sama ceremony
Rumi.fact: Upon his death, his followers and his son Sultan Walad set up the Mevlevi Order, also called the Order of the Whirling Dervishes, famous for the Sufi dance called the Sama ceremony.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: A hagiographical account of him is described in Shams ud-Din Ahmad Aflāki's Manāqib ul-Ārifīn (written between _____ and 1353)
Rumi.fact: A hagiographical account of him is described in Shams ud-Din Ahmad Aflāki's Manāqib ul-Ārifīn (written between 1318 and 1353).

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: According to Sultan Walad's Ibadetname and Shamsuddin Aflaki (c._____ to 1291), Rumi was a descendant of Abu Bakr
Rumi.fact: According to Sultan Walad's Ibadetname and Shamsuddin Aflaki (c.1286 to 1291), Rumi was a descendant of Abu Bakr.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The most complete genealogy offered for the family stretches back to six or seven generations to famous _____ jurists
Rumi.fact: The most complete genealogy offered for the family stretches back to six or seven generations to famous Hanafi jurists. The profession of the family for several generations was that of Islamic preachers of the relatively liberal Hanafi Maturidi school, and this family tradition was continued by Rumi (see his Fihi Ma Fih and Seven Sermons) and Sultan Walad (see Ma'rif Waladi for examples of his everyday sermons and lectures).

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: We do not learn the name of Baha al-Din's mother in the sources, only that he referred to her as "Māmi" (colloquial _____ for Māma), and that she was a simple woman who lived to the 1200s
Rumi.fact: We do not learn the name of Baha al-Din's mother in the sources, only that he referred to her as "Māmi" (colloquial Persian for Māma), and that she was a simple woman who lived to the 1200s.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: When the Mongols invaded Central Asia sometime between _____ and 1220, Baha ud-Din Walad, with his whole family and a group of disciples, set out westwards
Rumi.fact: When the Mongols invaded Central Asia sometime between 1215 and 1220, Baha ud-Din Walad, with his whole family and a group of disciples, set out westwards.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: He saw the father walking ahead of the son and said, "Here comes a sea followed by an ocean." _____ gave the boy his Asrārnāma, a book about the entanglement of the soul in the material world
Rumi.fact: According to hagiographical account which is not agreed upon by all Rumi scholars, Rumi encountered one of the most famous mystic Persian poets, Attar, in the Iranian city of Nishapur, in the province of Khorāsān. Attar immediately recognized Rumi's spiritual eminence.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: From Nishapur, Walad and his entourage set out for _____, meeting many of the scholars and Sufis of the city
Rumi.fact: From Nishapur, Walad and his entourage set out for Baghdad, meeting many of the scholars and Sufis of the city. From Baghdad they went to Hejaz and performed the pilgrimage at Mecca.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: When the Mongols invaded _____ sometime between 1215 and 1220, Baha ud-Din Walad, with his whole family and a group of disciples, set out westwards
Rumi.fact: When the Mongols invaded Central Asia sometime between 1215 and 1220, Baha ud-Din Walad, with his whole family and a group of disciples, set out westwards.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: From Baghdad they went to _____ and performed the pilgrimage at Mecca
Rumi.fact: From Baghdad they went to Hejaz and performed the pilgrimage at Mecca.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The migrating caravan then passed through _____, Malatya, Erzincan, Sivas, Kayseri and Nigde
Rumi.fact: The migrating caravan then passed through Damascus, Malatya, Erzincan, Sivas, Kayseri and Nigde.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: In _____, Rumi married Gowhar Khatun in Karaman
Rumi.fact: In 1225, Rumi married Gowhar Khatun in Karaman.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: They had two sons: _____ and Ala-eddin Chalabi
Rumi.fact: They had two sons: Sultan Walad and Ala-eddin Chalabi.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: On 1 May _____, most likely as a result of the insistent invitation of 'Alā' ud-Dīn Key-Qobād, ruler of Anatolia, Baha' ud-Din came and finally settled in Konya in Anatolia within the westernmost terr
Rumi.fact: On 1 May 1228, most likely as a result of the insistent invitation of 'Alā' ud-Dīn Key-Qobād, ruler of Anatolia, Baha' ud-Din came and finally settled in Konya in Anatolia within the westernmost territories of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rûm.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: For nine years, Rumi practised Sufism as a disciple of Burhan ud-Din until the latter died in _____ or 1241
Rumi.fact: For nine years, Rumi practised Sufism as a disciple of Burhan ud-Din until the latter died in 1240 or 1241.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: He also served as a Molvi (_____ teacher) and taught his adherents in the madrassa
Rumi.fact: Rumi's public life then began: he became an Islamic Jurist, issuing fatwas and giving sermons in the mosques of Konya. He also served as a Molvi (Islamic teacher) and taught his adherents in the madrassa.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: It was his meeting with the dervish Shams-e Tabrizi on 15 November _____ that completely changed his life
Rumi.fact: It was his meeting with the dervish Shams-e Tabrizi on 15 November 1244 that completely changed his life.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: It is essential to engage in discipleship to reach fana, the highest level of spiritual development in _____
Rumi.fact: It is essential to engage in discipleship to reach fana, the highest level of spiritual development in Sufism.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Shams had travelled throughout the _____ searching and praying for someone who could "endure my company"
Rumi.fact: Shams had travelled throughout the Middle East searching and praying for someone who could "endure my company".

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: There are many theories as to _____'s disappearance
Rumi.fact: Shams had travelled throughout the Middle East searching and praying for someone who could "endure my company". A voice said to him: "What will you give in return?" Shams replied, "My head!" The voice then said, "The one you seek is Jalal ud-Din of Konya." On the night of 5 December 1248, as Rumi and Shams were talking, Shams was called to the back door.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: He himself went out searching for Shams and journeyed again to _____
Rumi.fact: He himself went out searching for Shams and journeyed again to Damascus.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Rumi died on 17 December _____ in Konya
Rumi.fact: In December 1273, Rumi fell ill; he predicted his own death and composed the well-known ghazal, which begins with the verse: How doest thou know what sort of king I have within me as companion? Do not cast thy glance upon my golden face, for I have iron legs. Rumi died on 17 December 1273 in Konya.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: His death was mourned by the diverse community of Konya, with local _____ and Jews joining the crowd that converged to bid farewell as his body was carried through the city
Rumi.fact: His death was mourned by the diverse community of Konya, with local Christians and Jews joining the crowd that converged to bid farewell as his body was carried through the city.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: She was the one who sponsored the construction of his tomb in _____
Rumi.fact: She was the one who sponsored the construction of his tomb in Konya.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: It was from these ideas that the practice of whirling _____ developed into a ritual form
Rumi.fact: It was from these ideas that the practice of whirling Dervishes developed into a ritual form.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: His teachings became the base for the order of the Mevlevi, which his son _____ organised
Rumi.fact: His teachings became the base for the order of the Mevlevi, which his son Sultan Walad organised.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: In the _____ tradition, samāʿ represents a mystical journey of spiritual ascent through mind and love to the Perfect One
Rumi.fact: His teachings became the base for the order of the Mevlevi, which his son Sultan Walad organised. In the Mevlevi tradition, samāʿ represents a mystical journey of spiritual ascent through mind and love to the Perfect One.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: In this journey, the seeker symbolically turns towards the truth, grows through love, abandons the ego, finds the truth and arrives at the _____
Rumi.fact: In the Mevlevi tradition, samāʿ represents a mystical journey of spiritual ascent through mind and love to the Perfect One. In this journey, the seeker symbolically turns towards the truth, grows through love, abandons the ego, finds the truth and arrives at the Perfect.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The prose works are divided into _____, The Letters, and the Seven Sermons
Rumi.fact: The prose works are divided into The Discourses, The Letters, and the Seven Sermons.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The six-volume poem holds a distinguished place within the rich tradition of _____ literature, and has been commonly called "the Quran in Persian"
Rumi.fact: The six-volume poem holds a distinguished place within the rich tradition of Persian Sufi literature, and has been commonly called "the Quran in Persian".

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The style of the _____ ma fihi is colloquial and meant for middle-class men and women, and lack the sophisticated wordplay
Rumi.fact: The style of the Fihi ma fihi is colloquial and meant for middle-class men and women, and lack the sophisticated wordplay.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Majāles-e Sab'a (_____, Persian: مجالس سبعه) contains seven Persian sermons (as the name implies) or lectures given in seven different assemblies
Rumi.fact: Majāles-e Sab'a (Seven Sessions, Persian: مجالس سبعه) contains seven Persian sermons (as the name implies) or lectures given in seven different assemblies.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The sermons themselves give a commentary on the deeper meaning of Qur'an and _____
Rumi.fact: The sermons themselves give a commentary on the deeper meaning of Qur'an and Hadith. The style of Persian is rather simple, but quotation of Arabic and knowledge of history and the Hadith show Rumi's knowledge in the Islamic sciences.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: His style is typical of the genre of lectures given by _____ and spiritual teachers
Rumi.fact: His style is typical of the genre of lectures given by Sufis and spiritual teachers.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: As such, the _____ features as guidebook for humanity and those who want to understand the reality of the world
Rumi.fact: As Muslim, Rumi praises the Quran, not only as sacred book of Muslims, but also as tool to distinguish truth from falsehood. As such, the Quran features as guidebook for humanity and those who want to understand the reality of the world.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: One quatrain reads: _____ to the Quran, Muhammad is a mercy sent by God
Rumi.fact: Accordingly, Rumi criticizes Christianity for "overloading the image of God with superfluous structures and complications". One quatrain reads: According to the Quran, Muhammad is a mercy sent by God.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The Book conveys the prophets' circumstances those fish of the pure sea of _____
Rumi.fact: The Book conveys the prophets' circumstances those fish of the pure sea of Majesty.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: As respects to hunting through the treasure-trove of the Qur’ān, one can find in it [the _____ī] all [the Qur’ān's] ancient philosophical wisdom; it [the Mathnawī] is all entirely eloquent philosophy
Rumi.fact: On the first page of the Masnavi, Rumi states: "Hadha kitâbu 'l- mathnawîy wa huwa uSûlu uSûli uSûli 'd-dîn wa kashshâfu 'l-qur'ân." "This is the book of the Masnavi, and it is the roots of the roots of the roots of the (Islamic) Religion and it is the Explainer of the Qur'ân." Hadi Sabzavari, one of Iran's most important 19th-century philosophers, makes the following connection between the Masnavi and Islam, in the introduction to his philosophical commentary on the book: It is a commentary ...

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: He occasionally used the _____ language and single Turkish and Greek words in his verse
Rumi.fact: He occasionally used the Arabic language and single Turkish and Greek words in his verse.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: His poetry influenced not only _____ literature, but also the literary traditions of the Ottoman Turkish, Chagatai, Pashto, Kurdish, Urdu, and Bengali languages
Rumi.fact: His poetry influenced not only Persian literature, but also the literary traditions of the Ottoman Turkish, Chagatai, Pashto, Kurdish, Urdu, and Bengali languages.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Contemporary classical interpretations of his poetry are made by _____, Shahram Nazeri, Davood Azad (the three from Iran) and Ustad Mohammad Hashem Cheshti (Afghanistan)
Rumi.fact: Contemporary classical interpretations of his poetry are made by Muhammad Reza Shajarian, Shahram Nazeri, Davood Azad (the three from Iran) and Ustad Mohammad Hashem Cheshti (Afghanistan).

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences

Rumi.fact: So Rumi's first successor in the rectorship of the order was Husam Chalabi and, after Chalabi's death in 1284, Rumi's younger and only surviving son, Sultan Walad (d.

Rumi.fact: 1312), popularly called author of the mystical Maṭnawī Rabābnāma, or the Book of the Rabab was installed as grand master of the order.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: The music accompanying the samāʿ consists of settings of poems from the Maṭnawī and Dīwān-e Kabīr, or of _____'s poems
Rumi.fact: The music accompanying the samāʿ consists of settings of poems from the Maṭnawī and Dīwān-e Kabīr, or of Sultan Walad's poems.

Rumi.question: The centre for the _____ was in Konya
Rumi.fact: The centre for the Mevlevi was in Konya. The Mewlewī order issues an invitation to people of all backgrounds: During Ottoman times, the Mevlevi produced a number of notable poets and musicians, including Sheikh Ghalib, Ismail Rusuhi Dede of Ankara, Esrar Dede, Halet Efendi, and Gavsi Dede, who are all buried at the Galata Mewlewī Khāna (Turkish: Mevlevi-Hane) in Istanbul.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Music, especially that of the ney, plays an important part in the _____
Rumi.fact: The centre for the Mevlevi was in Konya. The Mewlewī order issues an invitation to people of all backgrounds: During Ottoman times, the Mevlevi produced a number of notable poets and musicians, including Sheikh Ghalib, Ismail Rusuhi Dede of Ankara, Esrar Dede, Halet Efendi, and Gavsi Dede, who are all buried at the Galata Mewlewī Khāna (Turkish: Mevlevi-Hane) in Istanbul.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: There is also a _____ī monastery (درگاه, dargāh) in Istanbul near the Galata Tower in which the samāʿ is performed and accessible to the public
Rumi.fact: There is also a Mewlewī monastery (درگاه, dargāh) in Istanbul near the Galata Tower in which the samāʿ is performed and accessible to the public. Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences

Rumi.fact: With the foundation of the modern, secular Republic of Turkey, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk removed religion from the sphere of public policy and restricted it exclusively to that of personal morals, behaviour and faith.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: On 13 December _____, a law was passed closing all the tekkes (dervish lodges) and zāwiyas (chief dervish lodges), and the centres of veneration to which visits (ziyārat) were made
Rumi.fact: On 13 December 1925, a law was passed closing all the tekkes (dervish lodges) and zāwiyas (chief dervish lodges), and the centres of veneration to which visits (ziyārat) were made.

Rumi.question: The law also provided penalties for those who tried to re-establish the _____
Rumi.fact: Istanbul alone had more than 250 tekkes as well as small centres for gatherings of various fraternities; this law dissolved the Sufi Orders, prohibited the use of mystical names, titles and costumes pertaining to their titles, impounded the Orders' assets, and banned their ceremonies and meetings. The law also provided penalties for those who tried to re-establish the Orders.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: Two years later, in _____, the Mausoleum of Mevlâna in Konya was allowed to reopen as a Museum
Rumi.fact: Two years later, in 1927, the Mausoleum of Mevlâna in Konya was allowed to reopen as a Museum.

Rumi.subject: Applied Sciences
Rumi.question: In the 1950s, the _____ government began allowing the Whirling Dervishes to perform once a year in Konya
Rumi.fact: In the 1950s, the Turkish government began allowing the Whirling Dervishes to perform once a year in Konya.

Rumi.question: In _____, the Whirling Dervishes were permitted to travel to the West for the first time
Rumi.fact: In 1974, the Whirling Dervishes were permitted to travel to the West for the first time.

Rumi.fact: Iranian musician Shahram Nazeri was awarded the Légion d'honneur and Iran's House of Music Award in 2007 for his renowned works on Rumi masterpieces. 2007 was declared as the "International Rumi Year" by UNESCO.

Saladin.fact: An important figure of the Third Crusade, he spearheaded the Muslim military effort against the Crusader states in the Levant.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Alongside his uncle Shirkuh, a Kurdish mercenary commander in service of the Zengid dynasty, Saladin was sent to Fatimid Egypt in _____, on the orders of the Zengid ruler Nur ad-Din
Saladin.fact: Alongside his uncle Shirkuh, a Kurdish mercenary commander in service of the Zengid dynasty, Saladin was sent to Fatimid Egypt in 1164, on the orders of the Zengid ruler Nur ad-Din.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: With their original purpose being to help restore Shawar as the vizier to the teenage _____ caliph al-Adid, a power struggle ensued between Shirkuh and Shawar after the latter was reinstated
Saladin.fact: Alongside his uncle Shirkuh, a Kurdish mercenary commander in service of the Zengid dynasty, Saladin was sent to Fatimid Egypt in 1164, on the orders of the Zengid ruler Nur ad-Din. With their original purpose being to help restore Shawar as the vizier to the teenage Fatimid caliph al-Adid, a power struggle ensued between Shirkuh and Shawar after the latter was reinstated.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: After Shawar was assassinated and Shirkuh died in _____, al-Adid appointed Saladin as vizier
Saladin.fact: After Shawar was assassinated and Shirkuh died in 1169, al-Adid appointed Saladin as vizier.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Not long after Nur ad-Din died in _____, Saladin launched his conquest of Syria, peacefully entering Damascus at the request of its governor
Saladin.fact: Not long after Nur ad-Din died in 1174, Saladin launched his conquest of Syria, peacefully entering Damascus at the request of its governor.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Saladin launched further conquests in northern Syria and Upper Mesopotamia, escaping two attempts on his life by the Order of Assassins before returning to Egypt in _____ to address local issues there
Saladin.fact: Saladin launched further conquests in northern Syria and Upper Mesopotamia, escaping two attempts on his life by the Order of Assassins before returning to Egypt in 1177 to address local issues there.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: By _____, Saladin had completed the conquest of Syria after capturing Aleppo but failed to take over the Zengid stronghold of Mosul
Saladin.fact: By 1182, Saladin had completed the conquest of Syria after capturing Aleppo but failed to take over the Zengid stronghold of Mosul.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Under Saladin's command, the Ayyubid army defeated the Crusaders at the decisive Battle of Hattin in _____, capturing Jerusalem and re-establishing Muslim military dominance in the Levant
Saladin.fact: Under Saladin's command, the Ayyubid army defeated the Crusaders at the decisive Battle of Hattin in 1187, capturing Jerusalem and re-establishing Muslim military dominance in the Levant. Although the Crusaders' Kingdom of Jerusalem persisted until the late 13th century, the defeat in 1187 marked a turning point in the Christian military effort against Muslim powers in the region.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Although the Crusaders' Kingdom of Jerusalem persisted until the late 13th century, the defeat in _____ marked a turning point in the Christian military effort against Muslim powers in the region
Saladin.fact: Under Saladin's command, the Ayyubid army defeated the Crusaders at the decisive Battle of Hattin in 1187, capturing Jerusalem and re-establishing Muslim military dominance in the Levant. Although the Crusaders' Kingdom of Jerusalem persisted until the late 13th century, the defeat in 1187 marked a turning point in the Christian military effort against Muslim powers in the region.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Saladin died in Damascus in _____, having given away much of his personal wealth to his subjects; he is buried in a mausoleum adjacent to the Umayyad Mosque
Saladin.fact: Saladin died in Damascus in 1193, having given away much of his personal wealth to his subjects; he is buried in a mausoleum adjacent to the Umayyad Mosque.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He has frequently been described as the most famous _____ figure in history
Saladin.fact: Alongside his significance to Muslim culture, Saladin is revered prominently in Kurdish, Turkic, Arab and even Western culture. He has frequently been described as the most famous Kurdish figure in history.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: His parents were of _____ ancestry, and had originated from the village of Ajdanakan near the city of Dvin in central Armenia
Saladin.fact: Alongside his significance to Muslim culture, Saladin is revered prominently in Kurdish, Turkic, Arab and even Western culture. He has frequently been described as the most famous Kurdish figure in history.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: His personal name was "Yusuf"; "Salah ad-Din" is a laqab, an honorific epithet, meaning "_____ of the Faith"
Saladin.fact: His personal name was "Yusuf"; "Salah ad-Din" is a laqab, an honorific epithet, meaning "Righteousness of the Faith".

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He was the son of a _____ mercenary Najm ad-Din Ayyub
Saladin.fact: He has frequently been described as the most famous Kurdish figure in history. His parents were of Kurdish ancestry, and had originated from the village of Ajdanakan near the city of Dvin in central Armenia.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Rawadiya tribe from which his family hailed were originally of Arab descent but later became _____
Saladin.fact: The Rawadiya tribe from which his family hailed were originally of Arab descent but later became Kurdicized.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, the defeated army of Zengi, Atabeg of Mosul, found their retreat blocked by the Tigris River opposite the fortress of Tikrit, where Saladin's father, Najm ad-Din Ayyub served as the warden
Saladin.fact: In 1132, the defeated army of Zengi, Atabeg of Mosul, found their retreat blocked by the Tigris River opposite the fortress of Tikrit, where Saladin's father, Najm ad-Din Ayyub served as the warden.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Ayyub provided ferries for the army and gave them refuge in _____
Saladin.fact: In 1132, the defeated army of Zengi, Atabeg of Mosul, found their retreat blocked by the Tigris River opposite the fortress of Tikrit, where Saladin's father, Najm ad-Din Ayyub served as the warden. Ayyub provided ferries for the army and gave them refuge in Tikrit.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Ayyub and his family moved to Mosul, where Imad ad-Din Zengi acknowledged his debt and appointed Ayyub commander of his fortress in Baalbek
Saladin.fact: In 1139, Ayyub and his family moved to Mosul, where Imad ad-Din Zengi acknowledged his debt and appointed Ayyub commander of his fortress in Baalbek.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: After the death of Zengi in _____, his son, Nur ad-Din, became the regent of Aleppo and the leader of the Zengids
Saladin.fact: After the death of Zengi in 1146, his son, Nur ad-Din, became the regent of Aleppo and the leader of the Zengids.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Another factor which may have affected his interest in religion was that, during the _____, Jerusalem was taken by the Christians
Saladin.fact: Another factor which may have affected his interest in religion was that, during the First Crusade, Jerusalem was taken by the Christians.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: More significantly, he knew the Hamasah of _____ by heart
Saladin.fact: More significantly, he knew the Hamasah of Abu Tammam by heart.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He spoke _____ and Arabic, and knew Turkish and Persian
Saladin.fact: He spoke Kurdish and Arabic, and knew Turkish and Persian.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Above all else he was a devotee of jihad: The sacred works [_____, hadith, etc.] are full of passages referring to the jihad
Saladin.fact: Above all else he was a devotee of jihad: The sacred works [Koran, hadith, etc.] are full of passages referring to the jihad.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Saladin ordered the arrest of a Sufi mystic, Qadid al-Qaffas (Arabic: قديد القفاص), in Alexandria
Saladin.fact: In 1174, Saladin ordered the arrest of a Sufi mystic, Qadid al-Qaffas (Arabic: قديد القفاص), in Alexandria.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, he ordered his son to execute the Sufi philosopher Yahya al-Suhrawardi, the founder of the Illuminationist current in Muslim philosophy, in Aleppo
Saladin.fact: In 1191, he ordered his son to execute the Sufi philosopher Yahya al-Suhrawardi, the founder of the Illuminationist current in Muslim philosophy, in Aleppo.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The answers to these questions lie in the kinds of _____ he wished to attract
Saladin.fact: Saladin welcomed Asiatic Sufis to Egypt, and he and his followers set up and endowed many khanqahs and zawiyas of which al-Maqrizi gives a long list. However, it is not yet clear what Saladin's interests in the khanqah actually were and why he specifically wanted Sufis from outside Egypt.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The founder stipulated that the khanqah be endowed for the Sufis as a group, those coming from abroad and settling in Cairo and _____
Saladin.fact: The founder stipulated that the khanqah be endowed for the Sufis as a group, those coming from abroad and settling in Cairo and Fustat.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: If those could not be found, then it would be for the poor jurists, either Shafi'i or _____, and Ash'ari in their creed
Saladin.fact: If those could not be found, then it would be for the poor jurists, either Shafi'i or Maliki, and Ash'ari in their creed.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Shawar, the vizier to al-Adid, who was the Fatimid caliph at the time, had been driven out of Egypt by his rival Dirgham, a member of the powerful Banu Ruzzaik tribe
Saladin.fact: In 1163, Shawar, the vizier to al-Adid, who was the Fatimid caliph at the time, had been driven out of Egypt by his rival Dirgham, a member of the powerful Banu Ruzzaik tribe.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He asked for military backing from Nur ad-Din, who complied, and in _____, sent Shirkuh to aid Shawar in his expedition against Dirgham
Saladin.fact: He asked for military backing from Nur ad-Din, who complied, and in 1164, sent Shirkuh to aid Shawar in his expedition against Dirgham.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: After the sacking of _____, the Crusader–Egyptian force and Shirkuh's army were to engage in the Battle of al-Babein on the desert border of the Nile, just west of Giza
Saladin.fact: Saladin's role in this expedition was minor, and it is known that he was ordered by Shirkuh to collect stores from Bilbais prior to its siege by a combined force of Crusaders and Shawar's troops. After the sacking of Bilbais, the Crusader–Egyptian force and Shirkuh's army were to engage in the Battle of al-Babein on the desert border of the Nile, just west of Giza.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Faced by a superior _____–Egyptian force attempting to besiege the city, Shirkuh split his army
Saladin.fact: Faced by a superior Crusader–Egyptian force attempting to besiege the city, Shirkuh split his army.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Shawar was reportedly assassinated by Saladin, and Shirkuh died later that year
Saladin.fact: In 1169, Shawar was reportedly assassinated by Saladin, and Shirkuh died later that year.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Following his death, a number of candidates were considered for the role of vizier to al-_____, most of whom were ethnic Kurds
Saladin.fact: Following his death, a number of candidates were considered for the role of vizier to al-Adid, most of whom were ethnic Kurds.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Their ethnic solidarity came to shape the _____ family's actions in their political career
Saladin.fact: Their ethnic solidarity came to shape the Ayyubid family's actions in their political career.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Having gained more power and independence than ever before in his career, he still faced the issue of ultimate loyalty between al-_____ and Nur ad-Din
Saladin.fact: Having gained more power and independence than ever before in his career, he still faced the issue of ultimate loyalty between al-Adid and Nur ad-Din.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Towards the end of _____, Saladin, with reinforcements from Nur ad-Din, defeated a massive Crusader-Byzantine force near Damietta
Saladin.fact: Towards the end of 1169, Saladin, with reinforcements from Nur ad-Din, defeated a massive Crusader-Byzantine force near Damietta.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: After establishing himself in Egypt, Saladin launched a campaign against the Crusaders, besieging Darum in _____
Saladin.fact: Afterwards, in the spring of 1170, Nur ad-Din sent Saladin's father to Egypt in compliance with Saladin's request, as well as encouragement from the Baghdad-based Abbasid caliph, al-Mustanjid, who aimed to pressure Saladin in deposing his rival caliph, al-Ad. After establishing himself in Egypt, Saladin launched a campaign against the Crusaders, besieging Darum in 1170.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Amalric withdrew his Knights Templar garrison from Gaza to assist him in defending Darum, but Saladin evaded their force and captured Gaza in _____
Saladin.fact: Amalric withdrew his Knights Templar garrison from Gaza to assist him in defending Darum, but Saladin evaded their force and captured Gaza in 1187.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____ Saladin destroyed the fortifications in Gaza built by King Baldwin III for the Knights Templar
Saladin.fact: In 1191 Saladin destroyed the fortifications in Gaza built by King Baldwin III for the Knights Templar.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: It is unclear exactly when, but during that same year, he attacked and captured the _____ castle of Eilat, built on an island off the head of the Gulf of Aqaba
Saladin.fact: After establishing himself in Egypt, Saladin launched a campaign against the Crusaders, besieging Darum in 1170. It is unclear exactly when, but during that same year, he attacked and captured the Crusader castle of Eilat, built on an island off the head of the Gulf of Aqaba.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Several Egyptian emirs were thus killed, but al-_____ was told that they were killed for rebelling against him
Saladin.fact: Several Egyptian emirs were thus killed, but al-Adid was told that they were killed for rebelling against him. While ill, he asked Saladin to pay him a visit to request that he take care of his young children, but Saladin refused, fearing treachery against the Abbasids, and is said to have regretted his action after realizing what al-Adid had wanted.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He died on 13 _____, and five days later, the Abbasid khutba was pronounced in Cairo and al-Fustat, proclaiming al-Mustadi as caliph
Saladin.fact: He died on 13 September, and five days later, the Abbasid khutba was pronounced in Cairo and al-Fustat, proclaiming al-Mustadi as caliph. On 25 September, Saladin left Cairo to take part in a joint attack on Kerak and Montréal, the desert castles of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, with Nur ad-Din who would attack from Syria.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: During the summer of _____, a Nubian army along with a contingent of Armenian former Fatimid troops were reported on the Egyptian border, preparing for a siege against Aswan
Saladin.fact: During the summer of 1173, a Nubian army along with a contingent of Armenian former Fatimid troops were reported on the Egyptian border, preparing for a siege against Aswan. Consequently, the Nubians departed; but returned in 1173 and were again driven off.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Consequently, the Nubians departed; but returned in _____ and were again driven off
Saladin.fact: During the summer of 1173, a Nubian army along with a contingent of Armenian former Fatimid troops were reported on the Egyptian border, preparing for a siege against Aswan. Consequently, the Nubians departed; but returned in 1173 and were again driven off.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: This time, _____ forces advanced from Aswan and captured the Nubian town of Ibrim
Saladin.fact: During the summer of 1173, a Nubian army along with a contingent of Armenian former Fatimid troops were reported on the Egyptian border, preparing for a siege against Aswan. This time, Egyptian forces advanced from Aswan and captured the Nubian town of Ibrim.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He did not press an attack against the desert castles, but attempted to drive out the _____ who lived in Crusader territory with the aim of depriving the Franks of guides
Saladin.fact: He did not press an attack against the desert castles, but attempted to drive out the Muslim Bedouins who lived in Crusader territory with the aim of depriving the Franks of guides.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On 31 July _____, Saladin's father Ayyub was wounded in a horse-riding accident, ultimately causing his death on 9 August
Saladin.fact: On 31 July 1173, Saladin's father Ayyub was wounded in a horse-riding accident, ultimately causing his death on 9 August.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In _____, Saladin sent Turan-Shah to conquer Yemen to allocate it and its port Aden to the territories of the Ayyubid Dynasty
Saladin.fact: In 1174, Saladin sent Turan-Shah to conquer Yemen to allocate it and its port Aden to the territories of the Ayyubid Dynasty.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On 15 May, Nur ad-Din died after falling ill the previous week and his power was handed to his eleven-year-old son as-_____ al-Malik
Saladin.fact: On 15 May, Nur ad-Din died after falling ill the previous week and his power was handed to his eleven-year-old son as-Salih Ismail al-Malik.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: When as-Salih was removed to _____ in August, Gumushtigin, the emir of the city and a captain of Nur ad-Din's veterans assumed guardianship over him
Saladin.fact: When as-Salih was removed to Aleppo in August, Gumushtigin, the emir of the city and a captain of Nur ad-Din's veterans assumed guardianship over him. In this emergency, the emir of Damascus appealed to Saif ad-Din of Mosul (a cousin of Gumushtigin) for assistance against Aleppo, but he refused, forcing the Syrians to request the aid of Saladin, who complied.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The emir prepared to unseat all his rivals in Syria and the Jazira, beginning with _____
Saladin.fact: The emir prepared to unseat all his rivals in Syria and the Jazira, beginning with Damascus. In this emergency, the emir of Damascus appealed to Saif ad-Din of Mosul (a cousin of Gumushtigin) for assistance against Aleppo, but he refused, forcing the Syrians to request the aid of Saladin, who complied.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: His army conquered _____ with relative ease, but avoided attacking Homs because of the strength of its citadel
Saladin.fact: His army conquered Hama with relative ease, but avoided attacking Homs because of the strength of its citadel.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On 11 May _____, a group of thirteen Assassins easily gained admission into Saladin's camp, but were detected immediately before they carried out their attack by Nasih ad-Din Khumartekin of Abu Qubays
Saladin.fact: On 11 May 1175, a group of thirteen Assassins easily gained admission into Saladin's camp, but were detected immediately before they carried out their attack by Nasih ad-Din Khumartekin of Abu Qubays.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Soon after, Saladin entered Homs and captured its citadel in March _____, after stubborn resistance from its defenders
Saladin.fact: Soon after, Saladin entered Homs and captured its citadel in March 1175, after stubborn resistance from its defenders.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Saif ad-Din mustered a large army and dispatched it to _____, whose defenders anxiously had awaited them
Saladin.fact: Saif ad-Din mustered a large army and dispatched it to Aleppo, whose defenders anxiously had awaited them. The combined forces of Mosul and Aleppo marched against Saladin in Hama.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On 13 April _____, the Zengid troops marched to attack his forces, but soon found themselves surrounded by Saladin's Ayyubid veterans, who crushed them
Saladin.fact: On 13 April 1175, the Zengid troops marched to attack his forces, but soon found themselves surrounded by Saladin's Ayyubid veterans, who crushed them.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Battle of Hama did not end the contest for power between the Ayyubids and the Zengids, with the final confrontation occurring in the spring of _____
Saladin.fact: The Battle of Hama did not end the contest for power between the Ayyubids and the Zengids, with the final confrontation occurring in the spring of 1176.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He reached the _____'s Mound, roughly 25 km (16 mi) from Aleppo, where his forces encountered Saif ad-Din's army
Saladin.fact: He reached the Sultan's Mound, roughly 25 km (16 mi) from Aleppo, where his forces encountered Saif ad-Din's army.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Zengid forces panicked and most of _____ ad-Din's officers ended up being killed or captured—Saif ad-Din narrowly escaped
Saladin.fact: He reached the Sultan's Mound, roughly 25 km (16 mi) from Aleppo, where his forces encountered Saif ad-Din's army. The Zengid forces panicked and most of Saif ad-Din's officers ended up being killed or captured—Saif ad-Din narrowly escaped.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Zengid army's camp, horses, baggage, tents, and stores were seized by the _____
Saladin.fact: The Zengid army's camp, horses, baggage, tents, and stores were seized by the Ayyubids.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He continued towards _____, which still closed its gates to him, halting before the city
Saladin.fact: He continued towards Aleppo, which still closed its gates to him, halting before the city.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: On the way, his army took Buza'a and then captured _____
Saladin.fact: On the way, his army took Buza'a and then captured Manbij.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The cap of his head armour was not penetrated and he managed to grip the _____'s hand—the dagger only slashing his gambeson—and the assailant was soon killed
Saladin.fact: Several days later, while Saladin was resting in one of his captain's tents, an Assassin rushed forward at him and struck at his head with a knife. The cap of his head armour was not penetrated and he managed to grip the Assassin's hand—the dagger only slashing his gambeson—and the assailant was soon killed.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Based in the an-_____, they commanded nine fortresses, all built on high elevations
Saladin.fact: Based in the an-Nusayriyah Mountains, they commanded nine fortresses, all built on high elevations.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: As soon as he dispatched the bulk of his troops to Egypt, Saladin led his army into the an-Nusayriyah range in August _____
Saladin.fact: As soon as he dispatched the bulk of his troops to Egypt, Saladin led his army into the an-Nusayriyah range in August 1176.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He saw that the lamps were displaced and beside his bed laid hot scones of the shape peculiar to the _____ with a note at the top pinned by a poisoned dagger
Saladin.fact: Saladin had his guards supplied with link lights and had chalk and cinders strewed around his tent outside Masyaf—which he was besieging—to detect any footsteps by the Assassins. He saw that the lamps were displaced and beside his bed laid hot scones of the shape peculiar to the Assassins with a note at the top pinned by a poisoned dagger.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He left _____ in command of Syria and left for Egypt with only his personal followers, reaching Cairo on 22 September
Saladin.fact: He left Turan Shah in command of Syria and left for Egypt with only his personal followers, reaching Cairo on 22 September.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Having been absent for roughly two years, he had much to organize and supervise in _____, namely fortifying and reconstructing Cairo
Saladin.fact: He left Turan Shah in command of Syria and left for Egypt with only his personal followers, reaching Cairo on 22 September. Having been absent for roughly two years, he had much to organize and supervise in Egypt, namely fortifying and reconstructing Cairo.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The city walls were repaired and their extensions laid out, while the construction of the _____ was commenced
Saladin.fact: The city walls were repaired and their extensions laid out, while the construction of the Cairo Citadel was commenced.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The chief public work he commissioned outside of Cairo was the large bridge at Giza, which was intended to form an outwork of defence against a potential _____ invasion
Saladin.fact: The chief public work he commissioned outside of Cairo was the large bridge at Giza, which was intended to form an outwork of defence against a potential Moorish invasion.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In November _____, he set out upon a raid into Palestine; the Crusaders had recently forayed into the territory of Damascus, so Saladin saw the truce as no longer worth preserving
Saladin.fact: In November 1177, he set out upon a raid into Palestine; the Crusaders had recently forayed into the territory of Damascus, so Saladin saw the truce as no longer worth preserving.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: The Christians sent a large portion of their army to besiege the fortress of Harim north of Aleppo, so southern _____ bore few defenders
Saladin.fact: In November 1177, he set out upon a raid into Palestine; the Crusaders had recently forayed into the territory of Damascus, so Saladin saw the truce as no longer worth preserving. The Christians sent a large portion of their army to besiege the fortress of Harim north of Aleppo, so southern Palestine bore few defenders.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: William of Tyre recorded that the _____ army consisted of 26,000 soldiers, of which 8,000 were elite forces and 18,000 were black soldiers from Sudan
Saladin.fact: William of Tyre recorded that the Ayyubid army consisted of 26,000 soldiers, of which 8,000 were elite forces and 18,000 were black soldiers from Sudan. On 25 November, while the greater part of the Ayyubid army was absent, Saladin and his men were surprised near Ramla in the battle of Montgisard (possibly at Gezer, also called Tell Jezar).

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: This army proceeded to raid the countryside, sack Ramla and Lod, and disperse themselves as far as the Gates of _____
Saladin.fact: This army proceeded to raid the countryside, sack Ramla and Lod, and disperse themselves as far as the Gates of Jerusalem.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Before they could form up, the _____ force hacked the soldiers of the Ayyubid army down by sword
Saladin.fact: Although the Crusader force consisted of only 375 knights, Saladin hesitated to ambush them because of the presence of highly skilled templar generals. Before they could form up, the Templar force hacked the soldiers of the Ayyubid army down by sword.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In the spring of _____, he was encamped under the walls of Homs, and a few skirmishes occurred between his generals and the Crusader army
Saladin.fact: In the spring of 1178, he was encamped under the walls of Homs, and a few skirmishes occurred between his generals and the Crusader army.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He spent the rest of the year in _____ without a confrontation with his enemies
Saladin.fact: He spent the rest of the year in Syria without a confrontation with his enemies. Saladin's intelligence services reported to him that the Crusaders were planning a raid into Syria.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: In April _____, the Crusaders and Templars led by King Baldwin expected no resistance and waited to launch a surprise attack on Muslim herders grazing their herds and flocks east of the Golan Heights
Saladin.fact: In April 1179, the Crusaders and Templars led by King Baldwin expected no resistance and waited to launch a surprise attack on Muslim herders grazing their herds and flocks east of the Golan Heights. In the summer of 1179, King Baldwin had set up an outpost on the road to Damascus and aimed to fortify a passage over the Jordan River, called Jacob's Ford, that commanded the approach to the Banias plain (the plain was divided by the Muslims and the Christians).

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: Baldwin advanced too rashly in pursuit of _____-Shah's force, which was concentrated southeast of Quneitra and was subsequently defeated by the Ayyubids
Saladin.fact: He ordered one of his generals, Farrukh-Shah, to guard the Damascus frontier with a thousand of his men to watch for an attack, then to retire, avoiding battle, and to light warning beacons on the hills, after which Saladin would march out. Baldwin advanced too rashly in pursuit of Farrukh-Shah's force, which was concentrated southeast of Quneitra and was subsequently defeated by the Ayyubids.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: He then resolved to destroy the fortress, called "_____" and defended by the Templar knights, moving his headquarters to Banias
Saladin.fact: He then resolved to destroy the fortress, called "Chastellet" and defended by the Templar knights, moving his headquarters to Banias.

Saladin.subject: Applied Sciences
Saladin.question: As the _____ hurried down to attack the Muslim forces, they fell into disorder, with the infantry falling behind
Saladin.fact: As the Crusaders hurried down to attack the Muslim forces, they fell into disorder, with the infantry falling behind. Despite early success, they pursued the Muslims far enough to become scattered, and Saladin took advantage by rallying his troops and charging at the Crusaders.
